results.proposal_summary: The Elsie Initiative Fund, administered through the UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office and supported by Canada, launched its Fourth Programming Round on 9 October 2025 to increase the meaningful participation of uniformed women in UN peace operations. The fund offers two modalities: Flexible Project Funding (FPF) for programmatic interventions and MOWIP Barrier Assessments for research into obstacles facing women in Troop/Police Contributing Countries. The Letter of Interest stage is now closed, and the current page serves only invited applicants proceeding to full proposal development. Eligible applicants are Troop/Police Contributing Countries and Participating UN Organizations. Grant amounts are denominated in USD; no maximum amount is specified. The call is not open to new applicants as of the current date.

theme: Decent Work in Crisis and Post-Crisis Situations
results.proposal_summary: This page is a BMZ press release dated 1 June 2026 describing a two-day visit to Lebanon by German Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan and her Norwegian counterpart. The visit focuses on the humanitarian situation of internally displaced persons and support for Lebanese government reform efforts. No call for proposals, funding instrument, eligibility criteria, or application deadline is present; this page does not constitute a grant opportunity.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The press release touches on humanitarian response and development in Lebanon but contains no call for proposals relevant to the ILO mandate.

results.exclusion_reason: This page is a press release announcing a ministerial visit, not a Call for Proposals. There is no open application window, no funding opportunity, no deadline, and no grant mechanism described.

results.title: BMZ Press Release: Strengthening Cooperation with Africa on Health – World Health Summit Kenya
results.organization: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
results.proposal_summary: This page is a BMZ press release dated 27 April 2026 reporting on Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan's visit to Nairobi for the World Health Summit Regional Meeting. It describes ongoing German-African health cooperation activities including pharmaceutical manufacturing support, epidemic preparedness, and malaria control, but contains no call for proposals, no grant funding mechanism, no eligibility criteria, and no application deadline.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The page covers health cooperation and job creation in Africa, with only marginal tangential relevance to ILO themes; it is not a funding opportunity.
